title: Closing: what the Jenkins orphanage made possible
summary: White credits the orphanage training for his career and the interview ends with thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well anyway, you've certainly explained a lot of things and directed a lot of false notions about music. I hope I have. I hope I have. Your broad experience is invaluable in being all over the country, which a lot of people have never had. That's right. Travel from one end of the country to the other and play and see everybody. Music all over the country. Thank you. It gives you a wonderful broad view of it.

Yeah. As near as I can give it to you, those are true happenings throughout my entire life. My encounter with the, or however these things would never have happened to me were, I committed to becoming an inmate of the Jenkins Orphanies. I have to credit the Jenkins Orphanies for the major happenings in my life. It was on account of me being an orphan, being admitted to the Jenkins Orphanies, being taken in there by the founder, that I enjoyed these privileges. Of course, the training I got in the Jenkins Orphanies furthered the success of these things. From the training they gave me, it allowed me to travel more extensively. Otherwise, I'd never been, if I had never studied the cornet or any music of any type, why, I'd never been found with any shows. Of course, my mother wanted me to be a preacher, and later years, some of the folks around wanted me to be a doctor, and for my part, I wanted to be a lawyer. And so then I discovered that there wasn't much for a lawyer to do. I didn't think he had much success.
